profile.synopsis: Bronwyn Paladin, from Potsdam, New York, is a graduate student in choral conducting at Lee University in Cleveland, Tennessee, where she began graduate studies in August 2026. A vocal performance graduate of Lee, she was named the university's 2026 Presser Undergraduate Scholar and has performed with its Chorale and Opera Theatre. She served as president of Ladies of Lee and received an Honorary Award in the Spring 2025 Aria and Concerto Competition. She gave her senior recital as a soprano on March 23, 2026, and was selected as a vocalist for the School of Music Senior Honors Concert.

profile.synopsis:
David Zufall is a wedding and portrait photographer based in Lisbon, New York, where his family farm, Robert Zufall Farm, operates as an organic dairy farm. His farm and nature photography from the Lisbon farm was featured in NCPR's Photo of the Day roundup on June 11, 2026. His work history includes supervisor roles at Yellowstone Airport and SkyWest Airlines, as well as work at Zufall Farm.

David Zufall Photography is a photography business based in Lisbon, New York, operated by David Zufall. It photographs weddings, portraits, and scenic and fine-art subjects throughout St. Lawrence County. NCPR featured its photograph of morning lambs at Zufall Farm in Lisbon.

profile.synopsis: Emmanuel Atindama is a mathematician who earned his MS in Mathematics from Clarkson University in 2022 and completed a PhD in Applied Mathematics there in December 2024. His research with Professor Prashant Athavale applies mathematical image processing and machine learning to electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) reconstruction, and he has published as first author in Integrating Materials and Manufacturing Innovation. He now works at Sokol GxP Services.

• Earned an MS in Mathematics from Clarkson University in 2022 (Clarkson University)
• His own CV lists his Clarkson PhD in Applied Mathematics as running September 2021 to December 2024 (Emmanuel Atindama CV)
• Co-author of a 2023 study on restoring noisy orientation maps from electron backscatter diffraction imaging, published in Integrating Materials and Manufacturing Innovation, volume 12, pages 251–266 (Clarkson University)

• The June 2025 Integrating Materials and Manufacturing Innovation paper he co-authored, on a hybrid algorithm for filling in missing data in electron backscatter diffraction maps, was selected for the editor's video summary (Clarkson University)

• Grace Serene is the stage name of Grace Levendusky (Roc City Magazine)
• Grace Serene and the Super Clean's lineup is Grace Serene (vocals), Zack Makida/Mikida (guitar), Arjun Baxter (bass), Joe Stehle (keys) and Brendon Caroselli (drums), and the band held its Super Clean Vol. 1 album-release show at Essex in Rochester on February 17, 2024 (Humanitix)
• Grace Serene grew up in Avon, NY, moved to Rochester in 2018, formed Grace Serene and the Super Clean in 2021 with Zack Mikida and Arjun Baxter (first song 'Slow Down'), performed at the Rochester International Jazz Festival, and moved to East Nashville in summer 2021 (Nashville Voyager)

profile.synopsis:
John Meyers, from Addison, New York, lives in Potsdam, New York. He is the owner and sole driver of Taxi Zero, a one-car taxi service based in Potsdam that has operated since 2014 and serves Potsdam, Canton, Ogdensburg, and Massena. He also owns Adirondack Apartments and publishes taxi-business content on TikTok and YouTube. He holds a Master of Science from Clarkson University.

JD's father. BS and MS from Clarkson University. Career arc: communications engineering, technical writing, internet marketing, then entrepreneurship. Owner-operator of Taxi Zero in Potsdam and Adirondack Quality Apartments; also runs short-term rentals and educational YouTube channels. Co-took the FAA Part 107 exam with JD in April 2018; both passed. Longtime Potsdam resident.

profile.synopsis: Josiah Martin is the owner-operator of Martin's Handmade Pretzels in Moira, New York, a fourth-generation family business that makes about six million handmade pretzels a year. profile.synopsis:
Dr. Michelle Johnston is an Associate Professor and Curriculum Coordinator in Criminal Investigation at SUNY Canton, where she also coordinates the Crime Analysis and Forensic Criminology curriculum. She holds a Ph.D. in Criminal Justice and Behavioral Science from Nova Southeastern University, an M.S. from Florida State University, and a B.A. from SUNY Potsdam, and previously spent five years with the New York State Department of Corrections and Community Supervision.

JD's most significant professor at SUNY Canton — taught Critical Issues in Criminal Justice (Fall 2020), Profiling and Behavioral Criminology (Spring 2022), and two sex offender courses (Fall 2022). Labeled JD "Person X" during the Profiling course — a designation for individuals who don't fit behavioral consistency models cleanly. Highly analytical, personally critical of law enforcement. Her ex-husband Herb Currier trained JD at the hospital; her son Dustin Currier was an instructor at JD's police academy. Served as a professional reference multiple times.

profile.public_footprint:
• SUNY Potsdam student from Canton, New York, majoring in Speech Communication; named to the Dean's List for Spring 2019 and Fall 2019 (SUNY Potsdam · Merit Pages)
• Studied Speech Communication at SUNY Potsdam and appeared on the Dean's List in Fall 2018, Spring 2019, and Fall 2020; from Canton, New York (SUNY Potsdam · Merit Pages)

• His van broke down in May 2021, leaving him without a vehicle that weekend. (iMessage record)
• Wrote film-journalism bylines for Hollywood Insider in 2020 (Hollywood Insider)
• His full name is Merrick William Sinclair. (Facebook Messenger)
• Born in May 1999. (Facebook Messenger)
• Lived in Madrid, New York, in his teens, at his parents' home, and attended Christian Fellowship Center's Madrid congregation. (Facebook Messenger)
• Was homeschooled as a teenager and attended Friday school classes, including a literature class, with school days typically ending mid-afternoon. (Facebook Messenger)
• Helped lead and organize a youth Bible study at Christian Fellowship Center in Potsdam in spring 2013, including arranging announcement publicity for it; his brother Jamie advised on the study's teaching approach. (Facebook Messenger)
• Played bass in worship at Christian Fellowship Center's Madrid congregation as a teenager. (Facebook Messenger)
• Ran media and AV for services at Christian Fellowship Center in Potsdam, including covering both services on a Sunday in March 2015. (Facebook Messenger)
• Played in a youth orchestra program in fall 2014, in the Allegro ensemble, and took lessons in the same program. (Facebook Messenger)
• Co-led publicity and outreach for Legacy, a youth conference hosted by Christian Fellowship Center, in August-September 2015, working alongside his father; the role involved personally inviting youth and coordinating promotion to about 13 area churches. (Facebook Messenger)
• Earned money as a teenager mowing and doing lawns for people and babysitting. (Facebook Messenger)
• Was writing fiction as a young teenager, including a book in 2012 and doing the writing for collaborative film projects with friends in 2013. (Facebook Messenger)
• Took a class involving graphic and logo design in fall 2016, with homework designing logos (initially in Canva, then as paper sketches at the teacher's direction). (Facebook Messenger)
• As of May 2015 he planned to attend SUNY Potsdam after graduating and to shift to Christian Fellowship Center's Potsdam congregation. (Facebook Messenger)
• His nephew Adrian is the son of his sister Louissa (Louissa Sinclair Tabolt). (Facebook Messenger)
• Served on the Legacy Board in 2015, helping plan the Legacy youth conference, including choosing worship songs; the group had spent about $573 on the conference by mid-September 2015. (Facebook Messenger)
• Took part in National String Project string lessons and a music recital in May 2015. (Facebook Messenger)
• Had a job with Friday hours in fall 2016, which limited his availability on Friday evenings. (Facebook Messenger)
• In 2013-2014 he helped produce and run the Christian Fellowship Academy event slideshows, including operating the looping slideshow. (Facebook Messenger)
• In late March 2014 he was playing in a band, with a band practice planned for the morning of March 28, 2014. (Facebook Messenger)
• Served on a yearbook staff in spring 2017. (Facebook Messenger)
• Had his own apartment in Potsdam by November 2019, hosting movie nights there. (Facebook Messenger)
• Started as a Communications Specialist with the New York State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation, Feb 2026 (The Morning Formation (Substack))

profile.synopsis: Michelle B. Larson became the 19th president of Clarkson University in Potsdam on April 1, 2025, the institution's first woman president. An astrophysicist by training, she earned her bachelor's, master's, and Ph.D. in physics from Montana State University, and previously served 12 years as president and CEO of the Adler Planetarium in Chicago and as vice provost of Utah State University.
profile.public_footprint:
• Michelle B. Larson was named the 19th president of Clarkson University in Potsdam, the institution's first woman president, beginning April 1, 2025 (Women In Academia Report)
• Before Clarkson, she served 12 years as president and CEO of the Adler Planetarium in Chicago and previously served as vice provost of Utah State University (Women In Academia Report)
• An astrophysicist by training, she earned her bachelor's, master's, and PhD in physics from Montana State University (Women In Academia Report)
• She completed postdoctoral work at Caltech, where she managed a geographically distributed cosmic ray experiment, and served as Deputy Director of a National Science Foundation Physics Frontier Center at Penn State. (Clarkson University)
• Celebrated her investiture as Clarkson University's 19th president on October 24, 2025, and launched her Dear Larson, for Clarkson inauguration letters project (Clarkson University)
• Serves on the American Physical Society's Panel on Public Affairs for a term running January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2026 (American Physical Society)
• Earned her doctorate in physics at Montana State University in 2001, with a dissertation on superfluid effects on the thermal evolution and rotational dynamics of neutron stars supervised by Bennett Link (Montana State University)
profile.highlights: Postdoctoral work at Caltech; Deputy Director of an NSF Physics Frontier Center at Penn State

profile.synopsis: Wayne Lougheed is Director of Safety and Security at St. Lawrence Health, which includes Canton-Potsdam Hospital, and has served as St. Lawrence Region Director of Security. He holds bachelor's degrees in Computer Science from William Paterson University and in Criminal Justice and Law Enforcement Administration from New Jersey City University, plus a 2004 police leadership and management certification through West Point. His earlier career in New Jersey included serving as a police lieutenant in Wayne Township, directing Northwest Bergen Central Dispatch, and consulting on security for Atlantic Health System.

• Most recently served as Director of Safety and Security at St. Lawrence Health (TheOrg)

record.title: Wayne Lougheed
record.body: Former police lieutenant from New Jersey. Director of Security at Canton-Potsdam Hospital when JD started in June 2023. Married to the hospital's Chief Nursing Officer. His leadership style — defending officers against vague complaints, using documentation as the department's defining strength, managing upward through visible metrics — made enough of an impression on JD that he wrote a formal case study on it. Resigned while JD was at BCT over a disagreement about badge-issuing duties being assigned to Security.

• Brings 16+ years of clinical experience, including 10 in inpatient mental health; New York State licensure and NBCOT registration since 2010; earned the CPRP credential in 2023; delivered a 2020 keynote for the Vermont Occupational Therapy Association (Clarkson University)
• Holds an OTD from Chatham University, a master's in occupational therapy and a bachelor's in health science from Utica College, and an associate degree as an occupational therapy assistant from SUNY Canton (Clarkson University)
• Trained in Dialectical Behavior Therapy and in the use of BTE equipment for functional capacity evaluations, pre-offer employment testing, and return-to-work assessments (Clarkson University · Merit Pages)
• Ashleigh Graveline serves as Chair of the Interprofessional Education (IPE) committee at Clarkson University, working to expand interprofessional learning opportunities for graduate healthcare students. (Clarkson University)
• Before joining Clarkson University, Ashleigh Graveline worked as an occupational therapist at Claxton Hepburn Medical Center, providing acute care ranging from general surgical recovery to orthopedics and outpatient therapy. (Clarkson University)
• Promoted from Clinical Assistant Professor to Clinical Associate Professor of Occupational Therapy in the Lewis School of Health Sciences at Clarkson University, 2022 (Women In Academia Report)
• Presented 'Navigating Tourette Syndrome in the School' to teachers and paraprofessionals at Kennedy Elementary School in February and September 2023. (Clarkson University)
• Holds a Car-Fit Certification (AARP and AOTA, 2020–present), an SBIRT Foundations Certification (2019–present), and a Physical Agent Modalities certification (2020–present). (Clarkson University)
• Presented on children's mental health diagnoses and suicide awareness and prevention at Heuvelton Central School, Mar 2025 (Clarkson University)
• Began a third Faculty Senate term at Clarkson University in 2025 (Clarkson University)
• Listed in the Arizona Occupational Therapy Association's 2025 conference program as Ashleigh Graveline, OTD, PhD, Assistant Professor and Academic Fieldwork Coordinator at Clarkson University (Arizona Occupational Therapy Association)

events.summary: iMessage exchange
Shared in the thread links about cameras for food photography, noting the recommended gear was expensive.
First iMessage contact on record

Shared in the thread that he had bought a Sony a6400 with a wide-angle lens primarily for video, discussed pricing for a photo project, and said Danica was the person to win over on photos, with costs clearly spelled out.
Told JD he had a business idea for him and asked for a call, then asked where he could find the photos JD had recently taken for them.
Shared in the thread that he needed a high-resolution pumpkin spice latte photo for the coffee business and suggested a test shot that JD could recreate with a better camera.
Asked JD whether a roughly 10MB photo file had been taken with his new camera and asked him to send the RAW version.
Told JD he had done post-edit work on a photo JD sent, found the original much duller, and said they needed a way to get higher-resolution files for poster-size use.
Reached out in general terms of personal support during a hard stretch, saying he was in JD's corner and was working through how to move forward.
Invited JD to stop by his office with no agenda, just to check how he was doing and processing things.
Asked JD to take his Highlander to Massena for a windshield replacement, laying out appointment options for the following week and a roughly three-hour appointment.
Confirmed in the thread a Friday 2 p.m. windshield appointment in Massena and noted JD would need to pay the deductible there, with Ryan providing a card.
Shared in the thread an update on a church-related appeal he had raised with elders in Madrid, in general terms, saying a follow-up meeting between two other men would shape the next step.
Offered JD paid cash errands, returning monitors to Walmart and taking items to a shipping place.
Asked JD to make an important first-stop delivery of four dozen bagels and assorted cream cheeses from the walk-in cooler to the Criscitello household.
Asked JD what he would charge to deliver Indian food, decided against it, said another friend would run it out instead, and offered JD a gift card for photos he had not yet had a chance to review.

Asked JD to photograph his coffee bags front and back, explaining there were 11 types in 3 sizes, that the 12-ounce size was probably enough, and that JD could set up at his office, with talk of a light box and filling the bags to reduce wrinkles.
Agreed in the thread to an easy first version of the coffee bag photos and a second round once his website shipped.
Asked JD whether he could drive Ryan's mother to the Syracuse airport the next morning in time for a 12:45 arrival.
Asked JD to deliver bagels to his house the next morning, three dozen from headquarters plus a specific bag of cream cheeses and lox portions waiting at the Potsdam store.
Arranged for JD to receive a $75 Park Bros card as payment for the coffee bag photos, saying another staffer would get it to him.
Asked JD about his availability and price to bring William home from the Boys and Girls Club in Ogdensburg the next night after a 6 p.m. finish.
Asked JD to drive Jameson to and from Christian Fellowship Center in Potsdam that day, leaving Madrid at 3:45 p.m. and returning at 6 p.m., then said he would ask JD's father instead.

Asked JD about delivering goods to Madrid that afternoon, balked good-naturedly at JD's $40 price compared with his teenage rates, decided to save the delivery for another day, mentioned Danica was expecting a baby, and congratulated JD on graduating.
Asked JD to extend his delivery the next day to drop bagels at Ryan's house for the morning, saying JD could bill the company for the difference and that the order would be bagged for him.
Thanked JD after the bagel delivery to his house in Madrid that morning, calling it a big blessing.

Asked JD in the thread to send her the dance from the previous night.
Asked JD in the thread to email her a copy of the tap dance number from Tuesday night, saying she would send it out to the whole class unless he had everyone's emails.

Coordinated in the thread for JD to record her tap and beginner ballet classes, working through the music and warmup list and a plan for JD to record near the end of the tap class and during the ballet class so he would not have to stay for the whole session.

Told JD in the thread she was sorry it had not worked out for him that semester and pointed him to Darlene, who was in charge of the financial side of things.
The thread's last exchange was a brief content-free message with a reaction, and nothing was left open.

First iMessage contact on record

Announced in the thread that David Woodard would be at the station the next day to hand out retention letters and discuss the closing of the station, and relayed word that Contour had not retained the OGS contract, with a retention bonus for staff who stayed through the contract term ending September 30.
Backed JD in the thread when his late arrival at the station was challenged as a safety issue, saying flooded roads had closed Route 11 between Canton and Potsdam and that he had JD covered.
Told the crew in the thread that anyone wanting to go to work with Trego-Dugan should send him their phone number and email address so he could pass them along to Katy.
Organized a final team lunch or dinner in the thread, asking everyone to settle on a day since it would be the last time they could do it as a complete team.
Posted a farewell thank-you to the crew for their hard work and dedication throughout their time at Contour, offering to serve as a professional reference for any of them.

directory.name: sf:kwadwo-appiah-kubi
directory.public_footprint:
• Clarkson's tenure announcement notes he joined in 2020, holds adjunct and courtesy roles in Ghana and Clarkson Biology, developed the VR-based GaitSIT assessment, and has 20+ peer-reviewed publications; office 2206 Clarkson Hall (Clarkson University)
• His awards include a Stanford Restore Center pilot award ($30,000) and an NIH Loan Repayment Program award ($50,000) (Clarkson University)
• Earned a PhD in Neuromotor Science from Temple University in 2019, an MS in Physical Therapy from Cardiff University in 2009, and a BS in Physical Therapy from the University of Ghana in 2005 (Clarkson University)
• Recipient of three NIH Loan Repayment Program awards, the NIH-funded Restore Center Pilot Project Award, and the American Physical Therapy Association New York Arthur J. Nelson Research Designated Fund Award (Clarkson University)
• Co-awarded a Clarkson CREST Graduate Assistantship for a proposal to redesign a low-power AI vision-controlled pediatric prosthetic hand (Clarkson University)
• Led a study of 133 adults ages 18–35, published in Applied Sciences, finding prolonged sitting and low activity weakened balance and walking even in healthy young adults (Medical Xpress)
• Led a study published in Methods and Protocols validating the GaitSIT virtual-reality walking-balance assessment in 29 healthy young adults across six sensory conditions. (Clarkson University)
• Serves on the editorial board of Physical and Occupational Therapy in Geriatrics and is a member of the American Physical Therapy Association, the International Society for Posture and Gait Research, and the Society for Neuroscience. (Clarkson University)
• Presented 'Retraining Balance: How the Brain Keeps Us Upright' at Clarkson University's Science Café in Potsdam on March 25, 2026, introducing the GaitSIT virtual-reality walking-balance assessment (Clarkson University)
• Co-authored a 2026 paper on Clarkson University's BOREALIS Scholars biomedical research training program for early-stage undergraduates in Biomedical Engineering Education, Mar 2026 (Springer)
• Co-authored 'Do Changes in Mental and Physical Energy and Fatigue Impact Changes on Neck Muscle Coordination?', published in Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise, Oct 2025 (Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise)
• Co-authored 'Association Between Leg Muscle Coordination and Subjective Energy-Fatigue States During Walking', published in Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise, Oct 2025 (Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise)

profile.synopsis: Kwadwo Appiah-Kubi is an associate professor of physical therapy at Clarkson University, with courtesy appointments in Biology and at the University of Health and Allied Sciences in Ghana. He joined Clarkson in 2020, earned his PhD in Neuromotor Science from Temple University in 2019, and previously earned physical therapy degrees from Cardiff University and the University of Ghana. His research centers on vestibular rehabilitation and postural control using virtual reality, including development of the Gait Sensory Interaction Test, and he has received NIH Loan Repayment Program awards and a Stanford Restore Center pilot award.

Maria told JD that Gabe had asked her to call him after class about JD, asked when JD wanted to start working, and days later proposed he start training during a closing shift with her and Lael.

Maria told JD she wanted to be careful about how a one-on-one outing would come across and suggested including Lael, while joking that she and Lael would plan a Mall of America graduation celebration for him.
Maria warned JD that a workplace photo involving Lael had been forwarded to Gabe, who had raised a concern about glove use when staff made food for themselves.
Maria pitched JD on delivering lunches for the Bagelry at his normal hourly rate while keeping all tips, roughly 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m., describing the lunch run as busy and successful.
Maria praised a video of JD's, loved the music choice, and urged him to watermark his work before sending it out so his name would get out there.

Whitney shared that she had just finished three lesson plans, loved being in Potsdam, was sad to go home soon and leave her friends, and felt school was heavy work but worth it for how much she was learning.
Whitney told JD she was graduating in May and asked whether he could take her graduation pictures on campus, hoping for sometime in mid-April when the weather was warm.
Whitney told JD she was sending her friend Cindy his information because Cindy was interested in having graduation photos done.
Whitney received her senior photos from the previous evening's campus shoot, called them gorgeous, and said JD could choose a few to feature on the website or she could.
Whitney met JD for a photo session at the Potsdam back parking lot at 5, then realized she had forgotten to pay him and asked for his Venmo.
The thread's last exchange left Whitney giving JD open permission to use photos from their SUNY shoot in a photography promotion graphic, saying he could use whatever, whenever.

profile.synopsis: Cassandra Fernandez is a captain in the New York Army National Guard and the officer in charge of the S1 section at Headquarters and Headquarters Company, 427th Brigade Support Battalion, in Syracuse. She enlisted as a human resources specialist in 2014, commissioned as a medical branch officer in 2018, and spent several years in medical readiness roles, including State Medical Readiness Officer, before moving into personnel leadership; since February 2024 she has served as a deputy brigade S1 while also serving as a battalion S1. She lives in the Syracuse area and teaches yoga at Salt City Holistic Health, where she leads Slow Flow classes and a monthly Yin with Reiki session; she completed her 200-hour yoga teacher training at Jai Yoga School and is a Reiki practitioner.
